pages.title: Planting and harvesting
pages.text: Plant a seed on tilled soil. In season it ripens in 1 to 2 MC days (3.5 to 5 out of season). At maturity, the harvest gives the crop and 1 to 2 seeds. On new soil: about 11 harvests for tomato or corn, 16 for soybean. Right-click a ripe crop with an empty hand: harvest and replant.

pages.title: Summer crops
pages.text: Tomato, corn, soybean, bell pepper, eggplant and cucumber have their optimal season in summer. In spring they are possible, in autumn unfavorable. Soybean is a legume that enriches the soil with nitrogen.

pages.title: Spring and autumn
pages.text: In spring: lettuce, onion, strawberry and barley. In autumn: garlic and cabbage. In winter, garlic, cabbage and onion stay unfavorable; the others do not grow outdoors.

pages.title: Greenhouses and winter
pages.text: A greenhouse gives a winter multiplier of 0.6 instead of 0.15 outdoors. Under glass, winter counts as spring when choosing crops, so spring crops can grow there.

pages.title: Irrigation
pages.text: The copper sprinkler (radius 2) and the iron sprinkler (radius 3) wet the soil and speed growth by 10 %. They draw water from a source or a rain barrel. In summer, drought sometimes removes moisture.

pages.title: Rain barrel
pages.text: The rain barrel fills under open sky in rain, from a water bucket, or from a water bottle. A nearby sprinkler draws from it. An empty watering can refills at its tap, one level at a time.
